newsitem.title: FRANCE: Russians angry after Chechens attend Euro-hearing.
newsitem.headline: Russians angry after Chechens attend Euro-hearing.

text.p: A Russian parliamentarian complained of meddling in Moscow's internal affairs on Tuesday after Chechen separatists were allowed into a hearing of the Council of Europe's parliamentary assembly.
"There has been a plot. We are astonished, even flabbergasted, by the disregard shown for the parliamentary assembly's decisions," said Vladimir Lukin, head of the assembly's Russian delegation.

He spoke to reporters after a delegation of four Chechens visiting the council in Strasbourg, northern France, were invited on Tuesday morning into a hearing of its parliamentary assembly's legal affairs committee.
A day earlier, assembly speaker Leni Fischer had limited the delegation during its visit to informal contacts with individual assembly members.

"I don't believe the king of Spain would come to the Council of Europe to hold talks with Basque separatists," snapped Lukin, who is the liberal chairman of the Russian parliament's foreign affairs committee.

The low-ranking Chechen delegation had arrived in Strasbourg on Monday despite the cancellation of an assembly hearing scheduled for Monday to discuss the peace deal for the breakaway Russian region signed on August 31.
The hearing was cancelled after Russian security tsar Alexander Lebed and Chechen separatist chief of staff Aslan Maskhadov both spurned council invitations to attend.
The Kremlin had blasted the invitation to Maskhadov as interference in Russian affairs.

Russia joined the 39-nation Council of Europe in February only after Moscow pledged to seek a peaceful settlement in Chechnya. The council was set up after World War Two to promote democracy and human rights across Europe.
